chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Sama'ah, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'If a servant upon whom Allah has bestowed a favor, whether he was ill or tested with a calamity, and Allah bestowed favor upon him again by curing him from that calamity, and he made it upon himself to give a vow (haram) for Khorasan, then it is incumbent upon him to complete it.'

key_terms.خُرَاسَانَ: Khorasan (a region in Persia, often used in hadith to denote a place of pilgrimage or specific worship)
key_terms.يُحْرِمَ: to vow/make obligatory upon oneself (from ihram context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a vow made for gratitude after being cured from illness?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the binding nature of conditional vows (*nadhr*) made in gratitude for deliverance from illness or calamity, emphasizing that the specific act vowed must be completed even if the devotee is elsewhere. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that a vow becomes obligatory upon the occurrence of the condition, reflecting the seriousness of fulfilling one's word to God as a form of thanksgiving (*shukr*).
